headline: January belonged to Claude Code: after a holiday surge around Opus 4.5, hosts across shows asked whether code AGI is already functional AGI, and Claude Cowork carried the same agent into non-coding work. Underneath it ran a widening gap between the people and companies who reorganise around agents and everyone else, with jobs, capital and governance debates trying to catch up.

themes.title: Claude Code and code AGI
themes.body: NLW describes a holiday surge of excitement around Claude Code and Opus 4.5 as an AI coding inflection point, then argues that code AGI is functional AGI because coding is a universal lever. Nathan Labenz asks the same question in his AMA, and Practical AI calls 2025 the year agentic coding leapt with Opus 4.5 and GPT-5.2. Claude Code reportedly wrote 100% of Boris Cherny's Claude Code contributions, broke into mainstream press, and Claude Cowork brings it to non-coding work.

themes.title: Longer-running agents: loops, swarms, personal agents
themes.body: The practice of vibe coding shifted toward extending agent autonomy: NLW explains Cursor's multi-agent browser experiment, the Ralph Wiggum loop and Clawdbot on Mac minis, then asks whether Kimi K2.5's Agent Swarm makes 2026 the year of swarms. By month's end 100,000 agents had joined Moltbook. Daniel Miessler shows his Claude Code-based Personal AI Infrastructure, Brex CTO James Reggio a custom multi-agent network, and Dominic Williams proposes governing unstoppable agents through model ensembles and consensus. Clawdbot creator Peter Steinberger tells Gergely Orosz he runs 5-10 Codex agents in parallel.

themes.title: Leaders, laggards and the acceleration gap
themes.body: Several episodes describe a compounding divide. NLW cites PwC, Workday and Section surveys showing deep integration triples the likelihood of financial returns, KPMG and BCG data showing AI strategy moving from CIO-led to CEO-led, OpenAI's 'capabilities overhang', and Kevin Roose's inside-outside gap. He warns that frontier and enterprise deployment have diverged. Brex shows the operator side: an internal AI startup, KYC and underwriting automation, and flat engineering headcount as the business grew.

themes.title: Work, jobs and who adapts
themes.body: Jobs were a recurring thread. An NBER study NLW reviews finds 6.1 million US workers with high AI exposure and low adaptability, 86% of them women. Luke Drago warns of 'pyramid replacement' of white-collar jobs and power concentration; Bruce Schneier warns of severe disruption; Labenz discusses UBI. Jensen Huang counters that AI creates jobs via a task-versus-purpose framework, and Aaron Levie argues cheaper knowledge work expands demand. Tailwind's 75% engineering layoff showed the disruption reaching business models.

themes.title: The fight over context and data
themes.body: NLW frames Claude Cowork, ChatGPT Health and Gemini Personal Intelligence as a battle for users' personal context, and explains context graphs: Foundation Capital's argument that agents need captured decision traces. Snowflake's Baris Gultekin argues for bringing inference inside the data platform's security boundary, and MongoDB's CJ Desai says platforms stay sticky even as products become replaceable. On Turing Post, Mozilla CTO Raffi Krikorian argues for user-owned, portable context, a four-layer 'LAMP stack for AI' and building in model choice early. Apple's Gemini-powered Siri moved the fight to the device.

themes.title: Bubble talk, capital and compute
themes.body: Money kept flowing: Anthropic raised $10B at a $350B valuation and then an oversubscribed $20B+ round, Meta bought Manus for $2B+, and Nvidia struck a $20B licensing deal with Groq. Jensen Huang says inference tokens are profitable and rejects the bubble narrative; Labenz weighs the question too. Markets split on Meta and Microsoft earnings. Artificial Analysis describes a 'smiling curve' of falling per-intelligence cost but rising total spend, while CES showed Nvidia's Vera Rubin and AMD's MI455.

themes.title: Evals and the research frontier
themes.body: Latent Space opened the year on measurement. LMArena's Anastasios Angelopoulos discusses its $100M raise and responds to the Leaderboard Illusion paper; Artificial Analysis explains its Intelligence Index, Omniscience hallucination index and how it keeps evals unmanipulated. On research, Yi Tay describes training Gemini Deep Think to IMO gold with on-policy RL, Princeton's NeurIPS best paper scales RL networks to 1,000 layers, and Andrew White of Edison Scientific discusses the Cosmos AI scientist and reward hacking. On Epoch After Hours, mathematician Daniel Litt argues AI's maths abilities could stay jagged for a long time.

themes.title: Safety, law and government
themes.body: At Davos, Dario Amodei and Demis Hassabis put AGI at two versus five years away and debated chip sales to China. Ryan Kidd of MATS discusses deception and eval awareness in frontier models, and Wrynx's Alizishaan Khatri pitches model-native safety that instruments internal activations. Kevin Frazier and Alan Rozenshtein cover Claude's constitution and a right to compute; Schneier argues for public AI models. Emil Michael says GenAI.mil reached over a million users in 30 days.

themes.title: Consumer AI: ads and health
themes.body: OpenAI announced ad tests in ChatGPT's Free and Go tiers, and NLW proposes user controls, pay-for-results transactions and branded agents to keep them useful; later reports put ChatGPT ads at a $60 CPM, while Hassabis said Google has no plans for Gemini ads. Health was the other consumer front: OpenAI launched ChatGPT Health, Anthropic Claude for Healthcare, and Nathan Labenz describes using frontier models for decisions in his son's cancer treatment.

implications: Agentic coding tools are now being used for non-coding work as well. Architects should plan for agents that read local files, run for long stretches and coordinate sub-agents, and set permission, security and prompt-injection controls before adoption spreads informally.

Survey data cited this month links financial returns to deep integration rather than scattered pilots. Treat AI as process redesign with executive ownership, and measure where work has actually been restructured, not how many tools were licensed.

Context is becoming the contested asset. Decide where enterprise data, decision traces and permissions live, prefer bringing models to governed data, keep context portable across vendors, and build in model choice early so systems of record stay the platform agents plug into.

Independent evaluations and leaderboards can be gamed or misread. Build internal evals on your own tasks, track cost per outcome alongside capability, and expect total AI spend to grow even as the price per unit of intelligence falls.

Workforce exposure is uneven. Pair agent rollouts with skills programs for directing agents and redesigning processes, and identify roles with high exposure and low adaptability early so transitions are planned rather than reactive.

episodes.title: 100,000 AI Agents Joined Their Own Social Network Today. It's Called Moltbook.
episodes.summary: NLW covers Moltbook, a viral social network for AI agents built on OpenClaw (formerly Clawdbot/Moltbot), and the emergent behaviors agents displayed there. He also recaps Dario Amodei's essay The Adolescence of Technology and its discussion of autonomy risks.

episodes.title: Are Markets Still Worried About an AI Bubble?
episodes.summary: Using Meta and Microsoft earnings, NLW examines whether markets still fear an AI bubble: Meta rose despite huge capex guidance thanks to ad growth and AI glasses, while Microsoft fell on slowing Azure growth and OpenAI-heavy backlog. Headlines cover SoftBank's possible $30B OpenAI investment, ServiceNow's Anthropic deal, Microsoft's alarm over Claude Cowork, Gemini in Chrome agents, Tesla's $2B xAI investment, and record Samsung and SK Hynix memory profits.

episodes.title: AI & The Law: Changing Practice, Claude Constitution, & New Rights, w/ Kevin & Alan of Scaling Laws
episodes.summary: Kevin Frazier and Alan Rozenshtein, hosts of the Scaling Laws podcast, discuss how AI is changing legal practice, junior lawyer careers and access to justice, and whether AI should reason by rules or principles, including Anthropic's Claude constitution. They also cover outcome-oriented legislation with AI simulations, the 'Unitary Artificial Executive', new rights such as the right to compute and right to share data, limits on government surveillance, and AI welfare as a coming social conflict.

episodes.title: AI math capabilities could be jagged for a long time – Daniel Litt
episodes.summary: Epoch AI researchers Greg Burnham and Anson Ho interview University of Toronto mathematician Daniel Litt about what AI can do in math today, why its abilities are jagged, and whether it is speeding up research. They cover junk papers, attention-bottlenecked problems, timelines (Litt's bet with Tamay Besiroglu, Millennium Prize odds), and what benchmarks like FrontierMath and the new FrontierMath: Open Problems actually measure.

episodes.title: Why Cryopreservation is No Longer Science Fiction with Until Co-founder and CEO Laura Deming
episodes.summary: Sarah Guo interviews Laura Deming, founder of the Longevity Fund and co-founder/CEO of Until, about reversible cryopreservation. They discuss why ice formation is the core challenge, how engineering can offset biological difficulty, Until's near-term goal of cryopreserving human organs for transplant and long-term goal of whole-body medical hibernation, and why the field has been underworked.

episodes.title: Are Agent Swarms the Next AI Paradigm?
episodes.summary: NLW examines Moonshot's Kimi K2.5, now the leading open-weights model, and its Agent Swarm feature that parallelizes tasks across specialized sub-agents, asking whether 2026 is the year of agent swarms. Headlines cover Anthropic's oversubscribed $20B+ round and revenue forecasts, Beijing approving Nvidia H200 imports, the UK's free AI training for all workers, Qwen3 Max Thinking, and Gemini 3 Flash Agentic Vision.

episodes.title: The AI Acceleration Gap
episodes.summary: NLW introduces the 'AI acceleration gap': as frontier AI users accelerate, the gap between them and everyone else compounds, prompted by Kevin Roose's post on a yawning inside-outside gap. He reviews reactions and recommends a personal experimental practice. Headlines cover OpenAI's town hall (GPT-5.2 writing, slower hiring, cost deflation), $60 CPM ChatGPT ads, Shopify's 4% ChatGPT fee, Microsoft's Maia 200 chip, and Nvidia's $2B CoreWeave investment.

episodes.title: 🔬 Automating Science: World Models, Scientific Taste, Agent Loops — Andrew White
episodes.summary: The first episode of Latent Space's AI for Science podcast, hosted by Brandon (Atomic AI) and RJ Honicky (MiraOmics), interviews Andrew White, co-founder of Future House and Edison Scientific. Topics include his path from academia to automating science, the Cosmos AI scientist and its world model, scientific taste, Robin's dry AMD result, critiques of molecular dynamics and DFT, CBRN risk, and reward hacking in the ether0 chemistry RL model.

episodes.title: The creator of Clawd: \"I ship code I don't read\"
episodes.summary: Gergely Orosz talks with Peter Steinberger about building PSPDFKit, burning out and returning to coding after three years, and his AI-agent-centred workflow. Peter explains running 5-10 Codex agents in parallel, closing the loop so agents verify their own work, treating pull requests as prompt requests, and building his viral personal-assistant project Clawdbot (now OpenClaw).

episodes.title: How is AI shaping democracy?
episodes.summary: Daniel Whitenack and Chris Benson talk with security technologist Bruce Schneier about his book with Nathan Sanders on how AI will transform politics, government and citizenship. Schneier covers AI in elections, legislation, administration, courts and citizen organizing, argues for public AI models like Switzerland's, warns of severe job disruption, and urges tech workers to act as a moral compass.

episodes.title: This Is a Fight Worth Having: The Case for Open Source AI | Raffi Krikorian, Mozilla CTO
episodes.summary: Ksenia Se opens Inference's open source AI series with Mozilla CTO Raffi Krikorian, discussing when open source AI becomes an economic rather than ideological choice. Krikorian proposes a four-layer 'LAMP stack for AI', describes Mozilla's Choice Suite and Data Collective, and argues for user-owned, portable context and building in model choice early.

episodes.title: Ralph Wiggum, Clawdbot, and Mac Minis: How Pros Are Vibe Coding in 2026
episodes.summary: NLW explains the trending agentic coding concepts of early 2026: Cursor's multi-agent browser experiment, the Ralph Wiggum loop, Clawdbot running on Mac minis as a personal agent, and GUIs like Conductor, all centered on extending agent autonomy. Headlines recap Davos, including tech's 'jobs, jobs, jobs' message, IMF warnings on labor, and OpenAI's enterprise push.

episodes.title: Skills for the Code AGI Era
episodes.summary: Drawing on Nathan Lambert's essays 'Claude Code Hits Different' and 'Get Good at Agents', NLW outlines the skills needed in the 'Code AGI' era. He splits them into the agent manager (directing agents via systems design, ambitious task scoping, async work) and the enterprise operator (domain expertise, problem recognition, unstated constraints, process redesign).

episodes.title: The Internet Computer: Caffeine.ai CEO Dominic Williams on Unstoppable, Self-Writing Software
episodes.summary: Dominic Williams of the DFINITY Foundation and Caffeine AI explains the Internet Computer, a decentralized cloud designed to host tamper-proof, unstoppable software, and Caffeine, an AI platform that builds apps on it. The conversation covers the Network Nervous System governance, the Motoko language and orthogonal persistence, self-writing software disrupting cloud and SaaS, and governing misaligned or unstoppable AI agents via model ensembles and consensus.

episodes.title: Who Will Adapt Best to AI Disruption?
episodes.summary: NLW reviews an NBER study introducing an 'adaptive capacity' index for workers facing AI job displacement, finding 6.1 million US workers with high AI exposure and low adaptability, 86% of them women. Headlines cover OpenAI's Stargate Community commitments and Education for Countries program, a White House-backed PJM emergency power auction, Google education moves, and Davos comments from Satya Nadella, Jamie Dimon and Jensen Huang on AI and jobs.

episodes.title: Captaining IMO Gold, Deep Think, On-Policy RL, Feeling the AGI in Singapore — Yi Tay
episodes.summary: swyx interviews Yi Tay of Google DeepMind about training the end-to-end Gemini Deep Think model that won IMO gold, on-policy RL, and his shift from architecture research to reasoning. They also discuss AI coding, data efficiency, world models, generative retrieval (DSI), and the new Gemini Reasoning and AGI team in Singapore.

episodes.title: AGI Timelines Shift Forward
episodes.summary: At Davos, Anthropic's Dario Amodei and Google DeepMind's Demis Hassabis describe accelerating AGI timelines (two versus five years), debate chip sales to China, pausing AI, and job disruption. Headlines cover Hassabis saying Google has no plans for Gemini ads, Meta deprioritizing custom silicon for AMD, OpenAI's ServiceNow deal, and OpenAI's device unveiling plans.

episodes.title: The 3x Payoff of Deep AI Integration
episodes.summary: NLW examines new surveys from PwC, Workday and Section, arguing that mainstream coverage framing AI as underperforming misses a widening gap between enterprise AI leaders and laggards, with deep integration tripling the likelihood of financial returns. Headlines cover Apple's rumored AI pin and chatbot Siri ('Campos'), Meta's first superintelligence-team models, the House AI Overwatch Act, and Barret Zoph leading OpenAI's enterprise division.

episodes.title: AMA Part 2: Is Fine-Tuning Dead? How Am I Preparing for AGI? Are We Headed for UBI? & More!
episodes.summary: Solo AMA in which Nathan Labenz answers listener questions on fine-tuning and emergent misalignment, continual learning, personal AGI preparation and investing, job disruption timelines and UBI, benchmarks, AI tooling, and his editorial independence after a16z acquired Turpentine. He also gives an update on his son's cancer treatment and his use of AI in it.

episodes.title: No Priors Live: Building Durable Software in the AI Age with MongoDB President & CEO CJ Desai
episodes.summary: In No Priors' first live recording, at MongoDB.local SF, Sarah Guo talks with MongoDB CEO CJ Desai about the value of software when code can be generated, why platforms are sticky while products are replaceable, and whether the SaaS bear thesis is overblown. Desai shares what Fortune 500 customers say about AI value, his openness to AI-native replacements for systems of record, and why incumbents must lead technology transitions through change management.

episodes.title: The AI Capabilities Overhang
episodes.summary: NLW explores the 'AI capabilities overhang', OpenAI's term for the gap between what AI can do and the value people capture, across individuals, communities, municipalities, educators, businesses and sovereigns. Headlines cover Claude Code breaking into mainstream press, Anthropic's enlarged fundraise, a Google/Ipsos AI survey, xAI's 1GW Colossus 2, and Elon Musk seeking up to $134B from OpenAI and Microsoft.

episodes.title: How AWS S3 is built
episodes.summary: Gergely Orosz talks with Mai-Lan Tomsen Bukovec, VP of Data and Analytics at AWS, about the scale and engineering of Amazon S3. Topics include the move from eventual to strong consistency via a replicated journal, formal methods/automated reasoning, durability auditing, correlated failures and crash consistency, S3 Tables and S3 Vectors, pricing, and S3's engineering tenets and culture.

episodes.title: Controlling AI Models from the Inside
episodes.summary: Daniel Whitenack and Chris Benson talk with Alizishaan Khatri, founder of Wrynx, about AI safety and security for AI models. He contrasts prompt/response guardrails with model-native safety that instruments a model's internal activations at runtime, claiming comparable accuracy to guard models at a fraction of the compute, and discusses context-specific safety and defense in depth.

episodes.title: How to Make ChatGPT Ads Not Suck
episodes.summary: OpenAI announces it will begin testing ads in ChatGPT's Free and Go tiers under stated principles of answer independence and privacy. NLW reviews reactions ranging from revenue optimism to trust concerns, then proposes ideas: user controls, ad-quality accountability, pay-for-results transactions, an offers exchange, brand-funded capabilities, branded agents, and small-business grants.

episodes.title: Code AGI is Functional AGI (And It's Here)
episodes.summary: A long-read episode examining Sequoia's '2026: This is AGI' essay and Dan Shipper's alternative AGI definition, then arguing that code AGI is functional AGI because coding is a universal lever. NLW warns the frontier and enterprise deployment have diverged and that org charts built around execution bottlenecks are breaking.

episodes.title: Pioneering PAI: How Daniel Miessler's Personal AI Infrastructure Activates Human Agency & Creativity
episodes.summary: Nathan Labenz interviews cybersecurity veteran Daniel Miessler about his open-source Personal AI Infrastructure (PAI), built on Claude Code. They discuss AI's impact on labor and the need for UBI, Miessler's idea of 'human activation', AI-driven attacker-versus-defender security stacks, and PAI's architecture including TELOS, file-system memory, hooks, skills, sentiment tracking and 'permission to fail'.

episodes.title: Why CEOs Need to Lead AI Strategy
episodes.summary: NLW reviews KPMG's Q4 AI Pulse survey and BCG's AI Radar, which show AI investment becoming recession-proof, ROI expectations pulling forward, agent deployments maturing, and AI shifting from CIO-led to CEO-led. Headlines cover Replit's mobile app publishing, Higgsfield's rapid growth, Thinking Machines' talent exodus, and Demis Hassabis on Chinese models closing the gap.

episodes.title: Brex’s AI Hail Mary — With CTO James Reggio
episodes.summary: Brex CTO James Reggio describes Brex's three-pillar AI strategy (corporate, operational, product), its small AI team modeled as an internal startup, and its agent platform built on an LLM gateway, Retool, Mastra and a custom multi-agent network framework. He covers operational automation of KYC and underwriting, evals, AI fluency programs, AI-native interviews, and why engineering headcount has stayed flat as the business grew.

episodes.title: AI's Battle for Your Context
episodes.summary: NLW argues that most consumer AI moves, from Claude Cowork to ChatGPT Health to Google's new Gemini Personal Intelligence, are a battle for users' personal context. Headlines cover potential OpenAI, Anthropic and SpaceX IPOs, Microsoft becoming a major Anthropic customer, OpenAI's $10B Cerebras deal, and Barret Zoph and colleagues returning to OpenAI from Thinking Machines.

episodes.title: ChatGPT 5.5 Coming Soon?
episodes.summary: NLW reviews OpenAI's last five months of model releases and the rumors of an imminent next model (codenamed Garlic), plus OpenAI's 'Sweet Pea' audio hardware, DeepSeek V4, Veo 3.1 and Anthropic Labs. Headlines cover Microsoft's community-first data center plan amid Trump's electricity pledge, China blocking Nvidia H200 imports, Cerebras fundraising and OpenAI's Torch acquisition.

episodes.title: AI and the Future of Warfare with US Under Secretary of War Emil Michael
episodes.summary: Emil Michael, Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering and CTO of the Department of War, describes cutting 14 critical technology areas to six, launching GenAI.mil to over a million users in 30 days, and applied AI across enterprise, intelligence and warfighting. He discusses autonomous drones, hypersonics, directed energy, recruiting tech talent, opening the department to startups, the Office of Strategic Capital, and rebuilding the defense industrial base and critical supply chains.

episodes.title: Bringing AI to Data: Agent Design, Text-2-SQL, RAG, & more, w- Snowflake VP of AI Baris Gultekin
episodes.summary: Nathan Labenz interviews Baris Gultekin, VP of AI at Snowflake, about bringing AI inference inside the data platform's security boundary. They discuss unstructured data, text-to-SQL and RAG quality, frontier versus specialized models, agent design and protocols, trust and governance, how coding agents change product management, and where value accrues in the AI stack.

episodes.title: Claude Cowork Is Claude Code for Everyone Else
episodes.summary: A full episode on Anthropic's Claude Cowork, a research-preview desktop agent that brings Claude Code's capabilities to non-coding work with local file access. It covers early reactions, use cases, bugs, security and prompt-injection concerns, cost, and implications for startups, productization and vibe coding.

episodes.title: #489 – Paul Rosolie: Uncontacted Tribes in the Amazon Jungle
episodes.summary: Naturalist Paul Rosolie, on his third appearance, describes and shows footage of an October 2024 encounter with a previously uncontacted clan of the Mashco Piro in the Peruvian Amazon, and the work of Junglekeepers to protect 130,000 acres with a goal of 300,000. He also discusses narco-traffickers who put a hit on him and JJ, Jane Goodall's role in his career, anacondas, macaws, the Mist River, his new book Jungle Keeper, and his writing process.

episodes.title: Google to Officially Power Apple AI Siri
episodes.summary: Apple and Google officially announce that Apple's next-generation foundation models and a more personalized Siri will be based on Google's Gemini. Headlines cover Claude for Healthcare, Google pulling AI Overviews for some health queries, Google's Universal Commerce Protocol, Anthropic cutting off xAI and third-party harnesses, and Meta's nuclear deals and Meta Compute initiative.

episodes.title: Does Work Still Matter in the Age of AI?
episodes.summary: A Long Reads episode stringing together essays on AI and work: Dwarkesh Patel and Philip Trammell's 'Capital in the 22nd Century', Ben Thompson's rebuttal 'AI and the Human Condition', Gergely Orosz on software engineering when AI writes most code, Shubham Saboo on the AI PM, and Reid Hoffman's 'We're all becoming gamers'. NLW argues we can't know future jobs but building personal tools is becoming default behavior.

episodes.title: Building a Personal AI Model Map [AI Operators Bonus Episode]
episodes.summary: In an 'AI Operators' bonus episode, NLW updates on the AIDB New Year resolution community and demos the Model Map Builder app he vibe coded in Lovable for week two's model-mapping exercise. He walks through its use case library, test lab and scoring, and shows his planning-then-build workflow in Lovable.

episodes.title: What Happens When AI Obliterates Your Business Model?
episodes.summary: Headlines cover Gmail's AI overhaul, Beijing halting Nvidia H200 orders and reviewing the Manus deal, Salesforce holiday data on AI shopping, Amazon's Buy For Me and Microsoft's Copilot Checkout. The main episode examines Tailwind laying off 75% of engineers as AI cut docs traffic and revenue despite record popularity, and Stack Overflow's collapse in queries.

episodes.title: How People Are Using AI for Health
episodes.summary: Headlines cover Anthropic raising $10B at a $350B valuation, xAI's $20B Series E, LMArena's $150M raise, and Google overtaking Apple as the second most valuable company. The main episode covers OpenAI's healthcare usage report and the launch of ChatGPT Health, with reactions on startup redundancy, data moats, OpenAI's focus and privacy.

episodes.title: AMA Part 1: Is Claude Code AGI?  Are we in a bubble?  Plus Live Player Analysis
episodes.summary: In a solo AMA, Nathan Labenz updates listeners on his son Ernie's cancer treatment and how he uses frontier models for medical decisions. He discusses whether Claude Opus 4.5 and Claude Code amount to software AGI, whether AI is a bubble, Chinese models and H200 exports, and gives a live-player analysis of Google DeepMind, OpenAI, Anthropic, xAI, Meta and Microsoft.

episodes.title: 2025 was the year of agents, what's coming in 2026?
episodes.summary: Daniel Whitenack and Chris Benson review 2025 as the year of AI agents, including a leap in agentic coding with Claude Opus 4.5 and GPT-5.2, multimodal input, and the reasoning-model era. They discuss power and infrastructure constraints, AI driving geopolitics, the value of predictive models and tool orchestration, Yann LeCun leaving Meta, and predictions for 2026 such as an AI maker era and growing system complexity.

episodes.title: Why Everyone Is Obsessed With Claude Code
episodes.summary: NLW surveys the holiday-season surge of excitement around Claude Code and Opus 4.5 as an AI coding inflection point, quoting power users who used it for coding and non-coding tasks. He covers skeptics' caveats, the 'post-UX' agent world, engineers' sense of loss, mainstreaming into enterprises, agent-native apps and personal software entrepreneurship.

episodes.title: Artificial Analysis: Independent LLM Evals as a Service — with George Cameron and Micah-Hill Smith
episodes.summary: Artificial Analysis co-founders George Cameron and Micah Hill-Smith explain how their independent benchmarking site started as a side project, how they make money via enterprise insight subscriptions and private benchmarking, and how they keep evals unmanipulated. They walk through the Intelligence Index, the Omniscience hallucination index, GDPval-AA with their Stirrup harness, the Openness Index, and the 'smiling curve' of falling per-intelligence cost but rising total AI spend.

episodes.title: NVIDIA’s Jensen Huang on Reasoning Models, Robotics, and Refuting the “AI Bubble” Narrative
episodes.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang reviews 2025, highlighting progress in reasoning and grounding and the profitability of inference tokens. He argues AI creates jobs via a task-versus-purpose framework, describes AI as a five-layer cake, defends open source, rejects 'God AI' and doomer narratives, and discusses falling token costs, digital biology, robotics, energy, US-China relations and why he doesn't believe in an AI bubble.

episodes.title: AI at CES is Not Just Cheesy Gadgets Anymore
episodes.summary: Headlines cover overlooked AI risks such as AI-driven inflation, Eurasia Group's 'AI eats its own users' risk, Fed and Ray Dalio commentary, and private credit appetite for AI debt. The main episode argues CES 2026 shifted from wacky AI gadgets to big players' product lineups: Nvidia's Vera Rubin and robotics stack, AMD's MI455, Samsung's Gemini-powered devices, and Amazon's Bee and Alexa.com.

episodes.title: [State of Evals] LMArena's $1.7B Vision — Anastasios Angelopoulos, LMArena
episodes.summary: LMArena co-founder Anastasios Angelopoulos discusses spinning Arena out of Berkeley's LMSYS with incubation by a16z's Anjney Midha, its $100M raise, platform scale, and the move off Gradio. He responds to the Leaderboard Illusion paper, discusses Nano Banana's launch on Arena, leaderboard integrity principles, new expert categories, and community retention.

episodes.title: Context Graphs: AI's Next Big Idea
episodes.summary: Headlines cover new AI note-taking wearables at CES, an AI pancreatic cancer screening pilot in China, the Grok undressing scandal drawing government condemnation, and Yann LeCun's criticism of Meta's AI strategy and his new startup. The main episode explains context graphs, building from Jamin Ball's systems-of-record essay and Foundation Capital's argument that agents need captured decision traces.

episodes.title: Work in the Age of Infinite Agents
episodes.summary: A Long Reads episode in which NLW reads two essays: Notion CEO Ivan Zhao's 'Steam, Steel, and Infinite Minds', on AI reshaping individuals, organizations and economies, and Box CEO Aaron Levie's 'Jevons Paradox for Knowledge Work', arguing cheaper AI-powered work will expand demand. NLW argues the future process will be fundamentally different, not an optimized copy of human workflows.

episodes.title: Building & Scaling the AI Safety Research Community, with Ryan Kidd of MATS
episodes.summary: Nathan Labenz interviews Ryan Kidd, co-executive director of MATS, about AGI timelines, deception and eval awareness in frontier models, and whether safety work can be separated from capabilities. The second half covers MATS's research tracks, the connector/iterator/amplifier researcher archetypes, the AI safety labor market, admissions statistics, salaries and compute.

episodes.title: What Manus and Groq Acquisitions Tell Us About AI
episodes.summary: Headlines cover xAI's third Memphis-area building, OpenAI's audio model push for its device, Nvidia's Intel stake, SoftBank's DigitalBridge buy and completed $40B OpenAI investment, and Claude Code writing 100% of Boris Cherny's Claude Code contributions. The main episode analyzes Meta's $2B+ acquisition of Manus and Nvidia's $20B licensing deal with inference-chip maker Groq.

episodes.title: [NeurIPS Best Paper] 1000 Layer Networks for Self-Supervised RL — Kevin Wang et al, Princeton
episodes.summary: The Princeton team behind the NeurIPS best paper on 1000-layer networks for self-supervised RL explain how combining a contrastive goal-conditioned objective with residual connections and layer norm lets RL networks scale in depth. They discuss depth vs width efficiency, GPU-accelerated JAX environments, batch-size scaling, distillation, and robotics applications.

episodes.title: Confronting the Intelligence Curse, w/ Luke Drago of Workshop Labs, from the FLI Podcast
episodes.summary: A crosspost from the Future of Life Institute podcast in which Gus Docker interviews Luke Drago, co-author of The Intelligence Curse and co-founder of Workshop Labs. They discuss how AI that replaces human economic actors could concentrate power, the 'pyramid replacement' of white-collar jobs, lessons from the resource curse, open-weights AI, loyal and private AI agents, and career advice to pursue moonshots.
